adjudications.decision: keep planning with a changed strategy
adjudications.why: Routine three-attempt budget spent, but the trajectory converged (3 blocking → 1 → 1) and each remaining finding was the residue of the previous fix rather than a recurrence. Round 3's own reviewer scoped the resolution as narrow and confirmed it does not reopen B4. Returning to an earlier phase would discard three rounds of confirmed-sound work for a mechanical gap.
adjudications.changedStrategy: Stop iterating the predicate against hand-picked attack lists — that is the failure pattern behind all three rounds. Require coverage proven over an ENUMERATION of TypeScript's export-surface grammar (a closed, finite set) rather than over a curated set of spellings.

adjudications.decision: keep planning with a changed strategy — FINAL adjudication available
adjudications.why: Round 4 confirmed the adjudicated enumeration strategy WORKS where it was applied: the export-surface axis (E1-E14) is now independently derived as complete, and the CommonJS exclusion verified sound. The remaining hole is that the enumeration discipline was applied to one axis only — export forms — and never to the binding-form axis, so the model's tracked universe silently narrows to initializer-carrying declarations. Round 4's reviewer scoped the fix as a completion of the same enumeration, explicitly not a fifth curated patch, and confirmed it reopens nothing already closed.
adjudications.changedStrategy: Make the predicate FAIL-CLOSED instead of fail-open. Four rounds have each found a spelling the tracked universe forgot, because the model enumerates what IS tracked — so every omission is a silent leak. Invert it: enumerate every way a module-scope name can be introduced (the full binding-form grammar), and default the mark universe to INCLUSIVE — any module-scope name that could hold a service value is tracked unless provably excluded. A future omission then surfaces as a loud false positive that fails the build, not as an invisible leak. Direction of failure is the structural fix; a fifth curated spelling list is not.
adjudications.consequenceIfFailed: Adjudication budget exhausted. Park as awaiting-human-review with the standing findings, both adjudications, and the R2 scope question below.

founderScopeQuestion.question: R2 (the launder rule) has now absorbed four critique rounds — every other part of this architecture passed. Is R2's full generality worth its cost, or should it be scoped to its founding case with the residue left as review territory?
founderScopeQuestion.context: R2 is a hardening beyond AC #3's literal text. refine-critique D3 established that WITHOUT some launder rule, AC #3 is vacuously satisfiable — today's core-api/src/index.ts:15 already satisfies it on paper. So a launder rule is load-bearing; the open question is how complete it must be to be worth shipping, given that the boundary itself holds by acquisition (independently verified) and does not depend on R2.
founderScopeQuestion.status: RULED 2026-08-08 — scope down. Verbatim: "lets avoid overengineering. we don't need to be able to catch every exotic catch, linting is engineering guidance not protection against malicious actors." and "keep it simple and focused no overengineering for things that don't matter in reality. hyperidle is a productivity tool without real users and we are currently cleaning up the architecture."

founderRulings.r2Scope: Reduced to the plain export-declaration shapes. R2 reads a module's export declarations; it does not read function-like bodies, class/enum/namespace members, mutation of an already-exported object, aliases, globals, or dynamic import(). Bypass-hunting apparatus deleted (E/N/F enumeration, fail-closed carrier model, loud kind guard, 54-case attack fixture, self-attack + residual fixtures, seven-run ceremony). No completeness claim is made. Applied in architecture §7.2/§7.3/§13.1 and feasibility P12; probe set reduced to 11 attacks + 6 controls, 4 runs.
founderRulings.b7: OUT OF SCOPE by the ruling, not fixed by code. Round 5's seven escaping-base mutation spellings all sit in the class R2 no longer reads. Nothing built for it.
founderRulings.supersessions: Both ratified — AU26 H1/H2's read-only door opens to port write ops; AU21 Decision E's SessionActivityBuffer relocates. No extra scaffolding.
founderRulings.atomicity: Relinquishment accepted at knowledge.ts:934 and threads.ts:1463; named failure windows stand; NO outbox or other durable mechanism — explicitly rejected as machinery for a failure that has not happened on a product with no real users.
founderRulings.split: Accepted — two work packages, sequential: wave A (core converses only through the door) then wave B (the applications compose faces). Each builds and verifies on its own.
founderRulings.applicationToLayerImport: Narrowing to face-shaped imports ratified as part of the face definition.
